successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: the remaining Etruscan cities between the Arno and the Tiber, allies of Rome from 264 (tint), citizens from 90

capitals.name: Velzna / Volsinii (Fanum Voltumnae, the league sanctuary)

ledger.x: 900 BC: 'The earliest evidence of a culture that is identifiably Etruscan dates from about 900 BC' (infobox 'Villanovan culture: 900 BC'); preceded by the 'Proto-Villanovan culture', which is no state.
650 BC: Padane Etruria.
600 BC: Campania.
550 BC: the Po plain to Spina and Adria.
540 BC: Corsica.
482-474 BC: the Veientine war.
474 BC: 'Veii sues for peace; tribute of grain and money', a '40-year truce'.

438-435 BC: Veii page: 'The nearby Roman colony of Fidenae revolted against Rome and allied itself with Veii'; Lars Tolumnus 'instigated a war with Rome in 438 BC'; the battle of Fidenae and 'a subsequent fiercely-fought battle with Veii in 437 BC' ended with Tolumnus killed.
435 BC: the Tolumnius war ends with Fidenae Roman again ('in the conquest of Fidene in 435 BC', Roman expansion in Italy).
424 BC: Capua to the Samnites.
406-396 BC: the siege of Veii.
396 BC: Veii falls.
396 BC: the siege ends with the capture of Veii.
396 BC: Emilia to the Boii.
396 BC: Lombardy to the Gauls.
396 BC: Adria.
391-390 BC: Volsinii's raid.
390 BC: the twenty-year truce.
384 BC: Corsica dropped (Cliopatria keeps it to 265).
383 BC: Sutrium and Nepet.
358-351 BC: the Tarquinian war.
351 BC: 'Tarquinii and Falerii granted forty-year truces', the 'End of the war (Livy)'.
310-307 BC: the Sutrium war.
307 BC: 'Three years afterwards' Publius Decius Mus 'captured several Volsinian fortresses' and the war lapsed; the page does not name the truces.
300 BC: '300 BC: Pyrgi becomes a Roman colony' (Etruscan civilization timeline): Caere's harbour on the coast.
298-295 BC: the Etruscan theatre of the Third Samnite War.
295 BC: after Sentinum and the defeat 'under the walls of their own city' (2,800 Volsinienses slain) the Etruscan cities fall out of the war; the pages give no truce terms.
283-280 BC: the last war.
280 BC: 'Coruncanius triumphs over Vulci'; Volsinii's wars 'ended in their final subjugation in 280 BC' (Volsinii page).
273 BC: Wars page: 'the Roman conquest of Caere in 273 BC' ('Brice (2014) argued the Roman conquest of Caere in 273 BC was the effective end').
265-264 BC: the Volsinii revolt and siege.
264 BC: Volsinii 'was destroyed by the Romans in 264 BC following an attempted revolt by its slaves'; the survivors were moved 'to a new city on the shores of Lake Bolsena' (Volsinii Novi).
264 BC: the siege ends; 'Resistance in Etruria was finally crushed in 265-264 BC' (expansion page).
264 BC: the end of independent Etruria.

wars.name: Battle of Alalia
wars.outcome: Phocaean 'Greek victory' at sea (Cadmean); the Phocaeans evacuate Corsica, 'captured by the Etruscans'; Sardinia stays Carthaginian

wars.name: Roman-Etruscan Wars
wars.outcome: 'Roman victory'; Veii destroyed 396, Caere taken 273, Volsinii destroyed 264

wars.name: Gallic invasion of the Po valley
wars.outcome: Gallic victory; Padane Etruria lost, Felsina becomes Boian

wars.name: Third Samnite War (Etruscan theatre)
wars.outcome: Roman victory at Sentinum (295) over 'a coalition of Samnites, Gauls, Etruscans, and Umbrians'

certainty.note: A league of city-states with no common frontier: the outer edge is the sum of the cities' territories as the archaeology suggests them.
The last year: the Volsinian siege and the dissolve.
